ai.literal: There is no fault in him, even though, sulking is capable of (increasing) the manner of his bestowing love.
ai.translation: Even though he has committed no fault, a lover's tiff has the power to increase the warmth of his affection.
ai.modern: அவரிடம் எந்தத் தவறும் இல்லை என்றாலும், அவரோடு ஊடல் கொள்வது அவர் தன் அன்பை வெளிப்படுத்தும் வழியை மேலும் சிறக்கச் செய்யும் ஆற்றல் கொண்டது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the playful nature of a lovers' tiff in classical love poetry. The heroine explains that even when her partner is completely faultless, feigning anger or sulking is highly effective. It has the unique power to enhance and sweeten the manner in which he showers his love and affection upon her during reconciliation. Thus, temporary sulking is portrayed not as a sign of discord, but as a delightful means to deepen their mutual intimacy.

ai.literal: The small resentment that arises from feigned anger, even if great affection withers, will obtain greatness.
ai.translation: The brief resentment that arises from a lover's tiff, even if it temporarily withers their deep affection, ultimately brings a greater beauty to their love.
ai.modern: ஊடலினால் உண்டாகும் சிறிய வருத்தம், நல்ல அன்பு தற்காலிகமாக வாடினாலும், முடிவில் பெருமையையே தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how a minor misunderstanding or feigned anger enhances love. The small resentment that arises during such a tiff might make their deep affection seem to wither temporarily. However, this brief period of distance actually intensifies their desire for each other. Ultimately, this experience gains greater value by making their reunion and subsequent love much sweeter.

ai.literal: Than sulking, is there a world of gods, inside those who are like water blended with the earth?
ai.translation: Is there a heaven of the gods that can offer greater joy than a lovers' tiff, for those whose hearts are blended like water with the earth?
ai.modern: மண்ணோடு நீர் கலந்து ஒன்றாவது போல இணைந்த காதலர்களின் நெஞ்சங்களுக்குள், ஊடல் கொள்வதை விட மேலான இன்பத்தைத் தரும் தேவர் உலகம் என்று ஒன்று இருக்கிறதா?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme pleasure of lovers' tiffs and their subsequent sweet reconciliation. The poet compares the intimate union of the lovers to water blending seamlessly with the earth, where the two elements become indistinguishable. For couples who share such a deep, inseparable bond of hearts, even the fabled heaven of the gods cannot offer a joy that surpasses the playful sulking of love. The key phrase 'nilattoṭu nīr iyaintannār' beautifully illustrates how their minds have merged into one, making their lovers' quarrels the ultimate source of delight.

ai.literal: Having embraced, without releasing, within the sulking, appears my heart-breaking weapon.
ai.translation: Within the very sulking that persists even as we embrace without letting go, there appears the weapon that breaks my heart.
ai.modern: தழுவிக்கொண்டு விடாமல் இருக்கும் ஊடலின் உள்ளே, எனது நெஞ்சத்தை உடைக்கின்ற ஆயுதம் தோன்றும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the intense emotional power of a lover's feigned anger or sulking (pulavi). Even when the lovers are in a tight embrace without letting go, a subtle sulking can still linger or arise within that intimacy. The speaker expresses that this persistent sulking acts like a sharp weapon, capable of breaking their heart. It beautifully illustrates how emotional vulnerability remains high even during physical closeness.

ai.literal: Even though they are without fault, from departing the soft shoulders of those whom one loves, in that state a certain pleasure it possesses.
ai.translation: Even though they are free of any fault, separating from the soft shoulders of the one we love has a unique pleasure of its own.
ai.modern: அவர்கள் எந்தத் தவறும் செய்யாதவர் என்றாலும், நாம் விரும்பும் காதலியின் மென்மையான தோள்களை விட்டு விலகி இருப்பதில் ஒரு தனி இன்பம் இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the sweet nature of feigned anger and temporary separation in love. The speaker explains that even when the beloved has done nothing wrong, there is a distinct, delightful pleasure in staying away from her soft shoulders for a brief moment. This distance is not caused by actual conflict, but is a playful pause that makes their eventual reunion even more joyful.

ai.literal: Even than eating, that which was eaten digesting is sweet; in love, than union, lover's tiff is sweet.
ai.translation: More delightful than eating is the digestion of what has been eaten; likewise, in love, more delightful than union is a lover's tiff.
ai.modern: உண்பதை விட உண்ட உணவு செரிப்பது இன்பமானது; அதுபோல, காதலில் கூடுவதை விட ஊடல் கொள்வது இன்பமானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the pleasure of love to the pleasure of eating. While eating is pleasurable, the true comfort and health come from the proper digestion of that food. Similarly, while physical union is pleasurable in love, the temporary feigned anger or lover's tiff (ūṭal) is even more delightful because it intensifies the desire and sweetness of the eventual reunion. The poet uses the physical process of digestion as a perfect analogy for how a tiff processes and enhances the relationship.

ai.literal: In feigned anger, those who yielded are the ones who won; that truth indeed in reunion will be seen.
ai.translation: In a lovers' tiff, those who yield are the ones who truly win; this truth will indeed be realized in the sweet reunion that follows.
ai.modern: ஊடலில் தோற்றுப்போனவர்களே உண்மையில் வென்றவர்கள் ஆவர்; அந்த உண்மை பின்னர் நிகழும் கூடலின் போது தெளிவாக உணரப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights a beautiful paradox in the intimacy of lovers. In a lovers' tiff or feigned anger (ūṭal), the partner who yields or 'loses' the argument is actually the true winner. By giving up their stubbornness, they initiate the end of the conflict. The truth of this victory is fully realized and felt during the immense joy of their subsequent physical and emotional reunion (kūṭal).

ai.literal: Having feigned anger, shall we obtain indeed, forehead to perspire, in the reunion that arose relish?
ai.translation: Will we ever obtain again, by feigning anger, that exquisite relish that arose during our reunion, which made her forehead perspire?
ai.modern: நெற்றியில் வியர்வை அரும்பும்படி நாம் கூடி மகிழ்ந்தபோது உண்டான அந்த இன்பத்தை (சுவையை), மீண்டும் நாம் ஊடல் கொள்வதன் மூலம் பெற முடியுமோ?
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the intense pleasure of reunion after a brief period of feigned anger (ūṭal). The word 'உப்பு' (literally salt) is used here in the sense of 'relish' or 'savoury delight', comparing the pleasure of love to the essential flavor that salt adds to food. The lover wonders if they can recreate that passionate moment of reunion—which was so intense that it made the beloved's forehead perspire—simply by starting another playful argument. It highlights how temporary disagreements serve to heighten physical and emotional intimacy.

ai.literal: Let her sulk indeed, she of bright ornaments, while I entreat; let it lengthen indeed, the night.
ai.translation: Let my beloved of bright ornaments prolong her feigned anger so that I may go on entreating her; and let the night also lengthen so that this sweet state may endure.
ai.modern: ஒளிரும் ஆபரணங்களை அணிந்த என் காதலி ஊடல் கொள்ளட்டும், அவளை நான் கெஞ்சி இரந்து சமாதானம் செய்யட்டும்; அதற்கு ஏதுவாக இந்த இரவும் நீளட்டும்.
ai.explanation: The speaker finds immense pleasure in the act of appeasing his beloved when she is feigning anger. He wishes for her to continue her sulking so that he can enjoy the sweet pleasure of begging for her grace. To allow this intimate play of love to continue without interruption, he also wishes for the night to stretch out and become longer. The particle 'manno' expresses a strong desire or wish, highlighting the intensity of his love.

ai.literal: Feigned anger to love [is] pleasure; to that, pleasure [is] if [one] gets to embrace having united.
ai.translation: Feigned anger gives pleasure to love; and the pleasure of that anger is to be united in a close embrace.
ai.modern: ஊடல் கொள்வது காமத்திற்கு இன்பம் தருகிறது; அந்த ஊடலுக்கு இன்பமாவது, மீண்டும் கூடித் தழுவப் பெறுவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This final couplet of the Tirukkuṟaḷ celebrates the sweet cycle of love. It states that a lover's feigned anger (ஊடுதல்) adds a unique pleasure to love (காமம்). However, that anger itself finds its ultimate pleasure (இன்பம்) only when the lovers reunite (கூடி) and embrace (முயங்க) each other. The word 'ஊடுதல்' refers to the playful sulking or tiff between lovers, which is not a real conflict but a prelude to deeper intimacy. Thus, the poet beautifully shows how temporary separation enhances the joy of union.
